purpose: Identify frequently weighted terms in high-rating and low-rating reviews.
strength: Simple, fast, interpretable, and useful for identifying salient vocabulary.
limitation: Does not capture deeper context, negation, sarcasm, or multi-word meanings well.
role_in_project: Provides baseline evidence for common language patterns in app reviews.

purpose: Assign reviews to predefined UX pain point categories using transparent rules.
strength: Highly transparent and easy to connect with UX categories and design implications.
limitation: Depends on manually defined keyword rules and may miss unexpected or implicit issues.
role_in_project: Translates review text into actionable UX pain point categories.

purpose: Discover interpretable latent topics within low-rating reviews.
strength: Reveals broader themes beyond individual keywords and complements rule-based categories.
limitation: Requires human interpretation of topics and can be sensitive to preprocessing and number of topics.
role_in_project: Validates and enriches the Level 2 pain point structure through unsupervised topic discovery.

purpose: Compare transformer-predicted review sentiment with user-provided rating groups.
strength: Captures contextual sentiment beyond keyword frequency and enables rating-sentiment disagreement analysis.
limitation: Sentiment labels may oversimplify mixed experiences and can be unreliable for short or ambiguous reviews.
role_in_project: Tests whether textual sentiment broadly aligns with rating-derived user satisfaction.

purpose: Assign low-rating reviews to UX pain point labels using a pre-trained transformer model.
strength: Can classify reviews into semantic UX categories without project-specific labelled training data.
limitation: Can produce high unclear rates and may be unstable when candidate labels do not fully match review language.
role_in_project: Provides a transformer-assisted comparison point for UX pain point labelling.
